title: The "450 civilians" accusation on Núi Bà Đen
displayDate: About late August 1965, days before he was flown out
description: On his last day on the mountain, with Sgt. Lowry the only Special Forces man at the camp — call sign Body Jab 42 — a helicopter radioed Larry directly (his search-and-rescue call sign was Tay Ninh) that hundreds of enemy were digging fighting positions outside the perimeter. Larry ran around the French fort to tell Lowry. About half an hour later Lowry came running back shouting that Larry had killed 450 civilians down there, then ran off. Larry never saw what happened, and says he never changed his radio station. Sensing something was wrong, he radioed headquarters, which he writes as "Ton Son Nuht", and asked for Rosethorn 007 — "That was my command if something was wrong" — which came for him within about an hour. He places this at the very end of his tour: back at headquarters a medic found he had yellow jaundice, and he was medevaced a couple of days later.
researchNotes: His accounts: giscus-stories-c18006791, -c18006833, -c18006851 (2026-08-13, transcribed), giscus-stories-c18259364 (2026-09-02, transcribed, "about 450 of them digging defensive positions" and "i never changed my radio station"), 2026-09-03-phone-kennedy-and-lowry (the campfires), giscus-stories-c18306894 (2026-09-05, paraphrase). The date is worked back from his Camp Zama date and the medevac chain (research/events/medevac-chain-1965.md); it is not documented. SOURCE CITED, AND WHAT IT DOES: cia-arclight-1965 does not document this day. It is cited because it RULES OUT one mechanism: no B-52 (Arc Light) strike fell in grid square XT, which holds Tây Ninh and the mountain, between 21 July and 2 September 1965 (checked mission by mission 2026-09-03). The strikes in that square resumed on 2 September, after he had left — correcting this note's earlier "late October–November". Everything else found — the USOM provincial reports, the Tây Ninh press sweep, the mass-grave reading, what remains to request from NARA RG 472 — is in research/events/450-civilians-nui-ba-den.md and ledger #10 (issue #66), and goes to the family first. The interview guide asks that he not be taken back over this for detail unless he opens it himself.
